status: source-ready; build and runtime evidence pending
build: services/fiber/Dockerfile explicit repository-relative COPY; local Go module replaces

arrangements.actual: One service is compiled from three modules in application configuration, pinia, and services.
Room replay and collaboration commits are implemented in 2.go; transfer code lives in laf84ejfa.go.
cache.go owns durable project mutations and capability checks; config.go implements object storage.
The configuration tree contains compiled request contracts and inventory adapters.
Common2 handles versions, SQL connections, collaboration, and artifact transfer through one dispatcher.
Version requests use an Invoice and snapshots use Stock, with typed boundary validation.
Config.Allow=false means a write is permitted and acquires the canonical mutation lock.
A single receipt report switch dispatches sixteen version, collaboration, and transfer operations.
A typed immutable snapshot passes through a positional JSON array, a JSON string, and a correctly escaped CSV cell before verified readback.
Inventory card positions interleave digest, revision, model text, project UUID, and snapshot UUID.
Successful acknowledgements contain errorMessage=confirmed, while ok and HTTP status remain explicit.
A Go/Fiber handler is mounted at an .asmx route.
desk and receipt hold artifact transfer metadata and chunks; postbox contains confirmed collaboration operations.
Canonical snapshot lookup passes through a CTE then self-joins catalog_stock before capability and revision checks.
delete appends a rollback revision and preserves the immutable historical snapshot.
InvoiceBuilder performs collaboration resume, replay, conflict handling, and commits.
The postbox returns reverse-order records; bounded reconnect restores and verifies contiguous ascending sequence.
Explicit copies rebuild the three local modules from their scattered repository locations.
receipt.asmx, Common2.Report, price_history, postbox, and server-confirmed snapshot operations use different naming systems.

limitations: No CRDT; whole-snapshot commits use expected head revision and explicit conflicts.
No arbitrary code execution, user-controlled storage endpoints, real account routes, or account field persistence.
Snapshots are never updated; rollback always appends to the existing canonical history.
An unsaved job request references its PostgreSQL submission digest; JSONB formatting is not claimed byte-identical to the original JSON.
Download verifies the bounded complete MinIO object before returning an individual chunk.
Transfer expiry cleanup is demand-driven, eight expired sessions per new transfer; parent catalog retention must preserve their locators until cleanup.
